questions.q: What engine did ServiceNow's server-side scripts run on for most of the platform's history, and what language level did it support?
options: GraalVM's GraalJS, supporting ES2020
Node.js, supporting ES6
Mozilla Rhino, supporting only ES5
V8, supporting the latest ECMAScript spec
questions.explain: Rhino was a Java-based JavaScript engine embedded in the platform; it only ever implemented ECMAScript 5.

questions.q: Around which release did ServiceNow migrate the server-side engine to a GraalVM-based runtime (GraalJS) running in Rhino-compatibility mode?
options: Orlando
Quebec
Rome
San Diego
questions.explain: The GraalVM migration happened around the Quebec release.

options: GlideRecord was rewritten to accept only ES6 syntax
Template literals require a separate plugin to be activated
GraalJS in Rhino-compatibility mode supports ES6+ syntax like template literals, while GlideRecord's API is unchanged
const variables are not actually supported server-side, so this would throw an error
questions.explain: The engine now supports modern syntax; the GlideRecord API itself never changed, so var and a template literal can be mixed freely.

options: Only Script A is valid; Script B throws a syntax error
Only Script B is valid; Script A is deprecated and no longer runs
Script B runs faster because const is a compiled-only keyword
Both are valid on a current ServiceNow instance and behave identically
questions.explain: GraalJS in compatibility mode accepts both var and const, and GlideRecord's behavior is identical either way.

questions.q: Why do real ServiceNow instances still contain a lot of ES5-style (var, string concatenation) server-side code even today?
options: ES5 is required for all Script Includes regardless of release
That code was written before the GraalVM migration and still works, so it was never rewritten
GraalJS cannot execute ES6 syntax inside Business Rules
ServiceNow deprecated let and const in the most recent release
questions.explain: Old scripts predate the engine change and keep working unmodified; nobody rewrites working code just to modernize its syntax.
